prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a temple was dedicated in 2000, the record year of 34 dedications.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country where at least one temple was dedicated in 2000, the record year of 34 dedications.
prompts.note: Counts only temples still listed as operating or in renovation; none from 2000 appear to have closed.
prompts.summary: The year 2000 set the record for temple dedications, with 34. Fifteen were in the United States and eight in Mexico, and five countries got their first temple: Bolivia, the Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Costa Rica and Fiji.

prompts.text_original: Pin a European country with a temple under construction but not yet dedicated (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church temple list and ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org (temples under construction), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, several European temples are under construction but not yet dedicated, including Birmingham England, Budapest Hungary, Vienna Austria, Brussels Belgium and Barcelona Spain. They will join older European temples such as Bern Switzerland (1955) and London England (1958).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where Saints places missionaries in the first big push abroad, 1849 to 1853.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 2 chs. 9 and 12 follow the Church's first big push of missionaries abroad, 1849 to 1853. Pin a country or territory where these chapters place missionaries at work.
prompts.citation: Saints vol. 2 ch. 9; Saints vol. 2 ch. 12
prompts.summary: Starting in 1849, Church leaders sent apostles and missionaries far abroad. Franklin D. Richards led the work in Great Britain, Erastus Snow went to Denmark, John Taylor to France and Lorenzo Snow to Italy. By 1853 missionaries had reached Cape Town and Tubuai in the South Pacific, and the Deseret News printed letters from Sweden, Australia and India.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Apostle Franklin D. Richards was sent to lead the work in Great Britain in 1849.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Erastus Snow went in 1849 with Danish Saint Peter Hansen, who reached Copenhagen in May 1850.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Apostle John Taylor was sent to France in 1849.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Lorenzo Snow went in 1849 with Italian Saint Joseph Toronto; the Deseret News later printed letters from there.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: The Deseret News printed missionary letters from Sweden.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: The Deseret News printed missionary letters from Australia.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: William Walker and fellow missionaries reached Cape Town in April 1853 and organized two branches.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: The Deseret News printed missionary letters from India.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: Louisa Pratt and other Saints sailed to Tubuai for the South Pacific mission.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that Saints names as home to a company of about 500 Saints sailing from Liverpool in the 1850s.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 2 ch. 15: a company of about 500 Saints that sailed from Liverpool in the 1850s came from these places. Pin one.
prompts.note: Saints says East India; mapped to India.
prompts.summary: In the 1850s a company of about 500 Saints sailed from Liverpool, England. Most came from Britain, but the group also included converts from Switzerland, Denmark, South Africa and East India, a sign of how far the gospel had already spread.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Most emigrants then came from Britain.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Danish converts sailed with them.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Swiss converts sailed with them.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: South African emigrants were in the company.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: Listed as East India.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country holding a Bible mountain whose site is agreed, or part of the land of Ararat.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a Bible mountain whose site is agreed, or part of the land of Ararat where the ark rested (Genesis 8:4)
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: Several Bible mountains can still be located today. Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel in Israel, and Moses viewed the promised land from Mount Nebo in Jordan before he died. Noah's ark rested on the mountains of Ararat (Genesis 8:4), the land of the ancient kingdom of Urartu, which at its height spread across parts of Turkey, Armenia, Iran and nearby countries.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Mount Carmel and Mount Tabor are in Israel.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Mount Ararat and the Urartian capital at Van are in eastern Turkey.

answers.name: Armenia
answers.fact: Yerevan grew from the Urartian fortress of Erebuni.

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Mount Nebo, where Moses viewed the promised land, is in Jordan.

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Urartu reached into north-west Iran around Lake Urmia.

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Mount Hermon's summit ridge lies along Lebanon's border.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Mount Hermon's summit ridge is shared with Syria.

answers.name: Azerbaijan
answers.fact: At its peak Urartu took in Nakhchivan.

answers.name: Georgia
answers.fact: At its widest Urartu reached southern Georgia.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Urartian lands touched the far north of Iraq.
